rules.reason: The CLI never reads a skill. Skills invoke the CLI, not the reverse — ADR-0004 puts deterministic logic in the CLI precisely so it does not depend on prose an agent interprets.
The CLI reads a workspace path given to it as an argument; it must not reach into .nit/ by convention, or it stops working on any project but this one.
Skills invoke the CLI for validation, archetype resolution and routing. This is the one dependency direction nit is built around.
Skills read and write workspace files at paths the supervisor supplies. Hard-coding .nit/ layout into a skill is what made the v1 skills unportable.
The workspace is project state and depends on nothing. ADR-0006: .nit/ holds what a project accumulates, not nit's own machinery.
Same as above. The duplicated .nit/skills tree deleted by ADR-0006 was exactly this dependency, and it went stale because nothing could see it was wrong.
